# Reordering tabs flashes every hidden tab into the header strip

## Context

Found in manual testing of `apps/workstation` on `dev` (2026-10-22): resorting tab headers in the pane that holds 12 tabs and an overflow `⋯`. In @tobiu's screen recording, two drops (at 32.4 s and 47.5 s) are followed by a 200–250 ms transient. The pane's header spans the whole frame with most of the 12 tabs in one row, the pane body goes black, and the neighbouring 100k Matrix pane disappears. Then the layout snaps back. The flicker and reflow reach well outside the pane being dragged in.

Further frames from the same recording, all inside one tab-drag operation (@tobiu's screenshots follow in a comment):
- **At about 36 s:** the header spans the full width with six tabs and the overflow `⋯` in one row. Its band styling is gone and the pane body is black.
- **Another moment:** the header looks normal ("Workspace Topology Inspector | Priority Alert Observatory"), but the neighbouring 100k Matrix grid is black.

## Measurements

Headless Chromium, 2200×1000, at `8bb3574d0f` (its `src/`, `apps/` and `resources/scss/` are identical to `dev` at `84b711878a`). A `requestAnimationFrame` sampler records the strip, its tab buttons, the pane and the 100k Matrix pane every frame.

| gesture | frames after release with > 4 tab buttons laid out | when | tab right edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| in-strip swap (2nd tab 180 px left) | 3 | +95 … +211 ms | **x 3032**, in a strip of x 1237–1863 |
| a drag with a 45 px rise out of the strip and back (2nd or 3rd tab) | 3–5 in each of 4 runs | +91 … +224 ms | x 3032 |
| drag into the pane body (no tab-set change) | 0 | — | — |

In those frames every one of the 12 tab buttons is in flow (`position: relative`) inside a 626 px strip. In this layout the strip, pane and grid rects stay unchanged, so headless it is a flash inside the strip.

The out-of-pane effects in the recording are **operator-observed, not reproduced headless**: the strip running over the neighbour, the band styling lost, the body and the neighbouring grid going black. Reading the frames, they are the same measuring window in a layout where the restored tabs overflow past the pane, and the grid blackout is the grid re-rendering after that reflow. That reading is inferred.

## The Problem

A reorder changes the tab set, so the overflow plugin recaptures natural widths. `Overflow#project(true)` step 1 puts every withheld header back into the **live** strip: `setSilent({hidden: false})`, `delete vdom.removeDom`, then `owner.promiseUpdate()`. It measures them with `getDomRect`, measures the strip extent in a second round trip, and only then applies the split again. Those are separate App↔main round trips, so the browser paints the restored state in between. The measuring window is visible for several frames on every reorder.

The plugin's own `@summary` says overflowing tabs "collapse behind one control whose menu reaches them". For the duration of the recapture they do not, and the user sees all of them.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`: `onTabSetChange()` runs `project(true)` for `insert`/`moveTo`. `project()` step 1 restores the withheld headers (comment: *"Restore them under this method's measuring latch, then reconcile their closest common parent once so getDomRect observes natural geometry"*), and step 3 / `applySplit` withholds them again.
- The natural-width cache is keyed by button id (`naturalWidths[button.id]`).
- Precedent for a measuring frame becoming visible: #19094 (a newborn split's overflow control flashed for one frame).

## The Fix

Measure natural widths without painting them in the strip:

1. **No live re-insert.** During the measuring window, restored headers take `position: absolute; visibility: hidden` (out of flow, unpainted, still at max-content width), or are measured in an off-strip layer. The live strip never shows them and never reflows.
2. **Recapture only what is missing.** A reorder changes order, not widths, and the cache is keyed by button id. Recapture only ids the cache lacks, such as newly inserted or re-created buttons. Check whether the dock's re-projection re-creates tab buttons on a reorder before relying on this.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a tab reorder, no frame lays out more tab buttons in the strip than the settled partition shows. No tab button paints outside the strip box at any point between release and settle.
- [ ] Inserting a tab still measures its natural width correctly: the partition after insert matches a fresh projection.
- [ ] **E2E:** a new spec under `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/` (e.g. `WorkstationTabReorderNoFlashNL.spec.mjs`) drives an in-strip reorder with a real pointer in the 12-tab pane and samples every frame (`requestAnimationFrame`) from release to settle. It asserts the visible-tab count never exceeds the settled count, and that the strip, pane and 100k Matrix rects stay stable. It must be red on `dev` (3+ frames with 12 tabs in the strip) and green with the fix, and it joins the hosted Workstation tier (#19655).
- [ ] `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL`, `WorkstationFocusedTabOverflowNL` and the overflow unit specs stay green.
- [ ] Post-merge, on the operator's setup: the recording's gesture shows no header band loss and no body or neighbour-grid blackout. If either persists with the measuring window fixed, it is a separate mechanism (e.g. the dock re-projecting the pane on drop). It then gets its own ticket, carrying the conditions that reproduce it, rather than reopening this one.

## Out of Scope

- Headers leaving the strip *during* the drag: #19988, a separate mechanism.
- #19982, the stale partition after maximize.

## Related

- #19094 (closed): a measuring frame made visible, the overflow-control case.
- #19982, #19984, #19986: the same testing pass, the same plugin and pane.
